observations: Photo 0 shows a used, disassembled car engine sitting on a dirty workshop floor, partly stacked with other engine cores.
Visible parts: intake manifold, injector rail, alternator, belt/pulley assembly, wiring harness, battery tray area — typical teardown photo of a 'Tokunbo' (Japan-used) engine.
No engine code, stamp, VIN plate, or any legible identifying marking is visible anywhere in the frame.
A watermark 'VICTOR NAZECO' and camera EXIF overlay are visible but these are not proof of the engine's identity.
Cylinder count and configuration cannot be confidently determined from the single angle shown — could be inline-4, V6, or V8 depending on what is hidden behind visible components.

identity.kind: used car engine, claimed Lexus LX460 (Japan import)

claims.evidence: No engine code, casting number, or Lexus/Toyota marking is visible in photo 0 to confirm this is a 1UR-FE (LX460/GX460) engine rather than any other used import engine.

risks.risk: Engine may not actually be a Lexus LX460 (1UR-FE V8) unit — could be a cheaper, smaller-displacement engine mislabeled to fetch a higher price.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the engine code/casting stamp (usually on the block near the bellhousing) or a VIN/parts tag.
risks.if_unproven: priced as an unidentified generic used engine, not as a premium Lexus V8 unit

risks.risk: Unknown mechanical condition — compression, oil leaks, timing chain wear, electrical faults are invisible in a static photo.
risks.proof: A start-up video with the engine running, showing idle sound and no visible leaks/smoke, plus a compression test reading.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working (worst case: non-running)

risks.risk: 'Japan engine' / low-mileage claim cannot be confirmed — no mileage sticker, auction sheet, or import documentation shown.
risks.proof: Photo of the Japanese auction sheet or import customs paperwork with mileage and grade.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified mileage/origin, not as a certified low-mileage import

risks.risk: Completeness of the engine (turbo, sensors, ECU, wiring harness) cannot be confirmed from one angle.
risks.proof: Multiple photos from all sides plus underside showing full block and accessory completeness.
risks.if_unproven: priced as possibly incomplete, missing accessories

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the engine code/stamp or casting number on the block.
A running/start-up video of the engine.
Photos from additional angles (rear, underside, opposite side) showing full engine and any ECU/harness.
Any import/auction documentation showing origin and mileage.
response.reason: The single photo shows a generic torn-down used engine with no readable code, stamp, or marking to confirm it is actually a Lexus LX460 (1UR-FE) unit; comparable prices for 'Lexus/Toyota V8' engines versus generic 4-cylinder engines differ by several million naira, so no meaningful worst-case price can be set without a legible engine ID shot.
